prompt: Edgar plays like a creature deck and folds to board wipes; I want life gain / life drain to be the ENGINE, not decoration — damage assigned outside combat through Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito and whatever doubles or increases it, and big evasive vampires (flying / lifelink / deathtouch) fast rather than a pile of generic 'vampires get +1/+1 when a creature dies' lords that wait for deaths nobody is causing. Stay bracket 3: NO two-card infinites. What do I cut, what do I add, and what should the sequencing of Vish Kal and Blood Artist be around a wipe? (Captain's log 006, 2026-09-29 at Oliver's.)
reading: The pilot's premise is measured and mostly right: in the 60-game standard-v3 run (V2, two swaps older than the sleeved v1.1.1: Elenda and Blade of the Bloodchief in, Immersturm Predator and Unbounded Potential out) our seat dealt 54.8 combat damage a game (ci95 [38.99, 70.61]) against 3.9 noncombat (ci95 [2.56, 5.24]), gained a MEDIAN of 5 life a game (mean 29.72, one 229-life outlier, ci95 [16.83, 42.6]), and kills landed as damage, not life loss — across all killers the three opponent seats in that run died by damage 85 times and by life loss 13. Read that as a floor, not a verdict: the record's own limits say a Vito or Blood Artist drain is life loss and never appears in a damage total, the Forge AI does not sacrifice for a benefit it cannot price, and it cast Vish Kal 0 times in 60 games; the goldfish cannot see the axis at all because `model_drain` is OFF and 11 drain cards (Vito, Sanguine Bond, Vish Kal, every lifelinker) are DARK to it. The wipe premise is three of six logged games filed `wipe` (001, 002, 006), and the audit's answer is not 'more protection' — protection is 7 copies, AT its 5–7 target, held by turn six in 51.6% of goldfish games, and log 002 records two of them uncast for mana — it is sweepers 0 (target 1–3) and a death-drain component of exactly two cards (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant; 37.1% drawn, 25.2% by turn six). The deck has no wipe of its own to make the deaths happen and only two cards that pay when they do. The 'pile of generic lords that wait for deaths' is smaller than the note thinks — enumerated from cards.json, exactly four cards carry a 'when a creature dies' pump trigger (Cordial Vampire, Elenda, Blade of the Bloodchief, Yahenni — Yahenni only on an OPPONENT'S creature) and four static creature lords (Legion Lieutenant, Captivating Vampire, Stromkirk Captain, Lord of Lineage's back face) plus two noncreature anthems (Patchwork Banner, Caretaker's Talent level 3); Elenda is the pilot's own 2026-09-16 add and dies into doubled lifelink tokens, so she is excluded from the cut pool. THE CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY BREACHED ON THE SLEEVED LIST: bracket_report puts the floor at 4 with `two_card_infinite` the signal that forces it, and both lines are checker-passed table-kills (stack 004 Conqueror + Vito, 13 resolutions; stack 006 Conqueror + Sanguine Bond, 13 resolutions). Bloodthirsty Conqueror is the one card common to both — it is the deck's ONLY loss-to-gain converter, so it loops with EVERY gain-to-loss piece (Vito, Bond, and any Cliffhaven Vampire / Marauding Blight-Priest you might add). Honouring 'no two-card infinites' therefore costs exactly one card and the whole class it belongs to: cut Conqueror and `bracket-check` recomputes the floor at 3 with zero infinites (the three Game Changers — Ancient Tomb, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor — sit at bracket 3's 'up to three' cap); keep him and the floor stays 4 whatever else is swapped. What the cut costs the drain axis: the deck's largest evasive body (one of three cards that enter as a 5-power flyer, with Vish Kal and High-Society Hunter), the 'SURVIVING INFINITE' engine target (assembled 7.8%, 3.4% by turn six — it was never the deck's clock), and the free lifegain half of every drain. What it buys: every gain-to-loss card in the corpus becomes a legal add, so lifelink bodies drain three times over. The two readings are ranked separately below (A: keep the pair, floor 4; B: cut Conqueror, floor 3) — the choice is the pilot's, and this document does not make it. SEQUENCING VISH KAL AND BLOOD ARTIST AROUND A WIPE, from the rules and the log rather than the note's lesson: Blood Artist goes DOWN BEFORE the wipe, not after it. CR 603.10a — leaves-the-battlefield triggers 'look back in time', and the rule's own example is 'Whenever a creature dies, you gain 1 life' surviving a destroy-everything spell and triggering per creature — so Blood Artist dying alongside eleven Vampires triggers twelve times (himself included), each 'target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life' — twelve points of drain the pilot distributes one target at a time, not twelve off each opponent; the TABLE-wide drain on a wipe is Cruel Celebrant's 'each opponent' (creatures you control), and Bastion's if added. Log 002 is the pilot's recollection of that turn — Artist and Conqueror out, eleven deaths, 'took every opponent for 11' — which cannot be Artist alone and is not a measurement of him; it is evidence that the pieces were on the table BEFORE the wipe, which is the sequencing point. Holding him for after the wipe throws that away; the reason to hold a two-mana Artist is a seat holding counters (Tom, log 001), not the wipe. Vish Kal is the opposite: seven mana with no self-protection, and against a DESTROY wipe sacrificing the team to him changes nothing about the death count (Blood Artist triggers either way) and the counters die with him. His sacrifice ability earns its keep in three cases only — an EXILE wipe (Farewell), a BOUNCE wipe (Cyclonic Rift, which log 001 names at Tom's), or a -X/-X wipe, where sacrificing in response manufactures the deaths the wipe would deny — and as the post-wipe rebuild, when the 'small blockers' the note describes become counters on a 5/5 flying lifelinker that Vito converts. So: Artist early, Vish Kal after the table's first wipe or only with Flawless Maneuver (free with Edgar out) or Boros Charm in hand — which is strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's 'keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper', and the pilot's own 'played it too early'. The exact stack is routed to resolve-stack below; nothing above is asserted as verified.

open_questions.question: Vish Kal, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant on the battlefield with six Vampires; an opponent casts (a) a destroy-all wipe, (b) Cyclonic Rift overloaded, (c) Farewell exiling creatures. In response the pilot sacrifices every other creature to Vish Kal. Per case: how many Blood Artist / Cruel Celebrant triggers fire, whether sacrificing changes the count against the destroy wipe (the reading above says it does not), how many counters Vish Kal holds, and whether he survives with and without Flawless Maneuver.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The sequencing answer in the reading rests on CR 603.10a's look-back and on the bounce/exile distinction; a checker-passed board makes it a procedure the handbook can print instead of a doctor's reading.

open_questions.question: Set `model_drain: true` in goldfish_targets.json (the same commit as any swap), so the eleven DARK drain cards — Vito, Sanguine Bond, Vish Kal, the lifelinkers, Crossway Troublemakers — are priced, and report life gained, life drained and noncombat damage by turn on the current list before and after the swaps. Which of the pilot's four asked-for measures ('life gained and life drained over the span of a game', 'damage assigned through Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Vito and anything that doubles it', 'average creature size', 'big scary vampires fast') does the model then produce, and which remain DARK?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every drain figure in this document is Forge's, on a list two cards older than the sleeved one, from an AI that never sacrifices and never cast Vish Kal. The goldfish is the instrument that can price a swap on this axis cheaply and on the current list — Forge reads life gained and lost only as a floor — and today it cannot see the axis at all.

open_questions.question: Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Cliffhaven Vampire: combo_details.json's by_card index lists it as a two-card infinite (Conqueror has twelve two-card partners there) and `bracket.assess` on the 99 plus Cliffhaven returns it as a contained line and the loop has the shape stack 006 verified (Bond's 'target opponent loses that much' against Cliffhaven's 'each opponent loses 1'). Is it deterministic and unbounded on the same terms, and does the mandatory 'each opponent' make it a table-kill with no choice to stop?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the reason Cliffhaven is ranked under reading B only; if the loop is not a kill the card is legal under A as well.

open_questions.question: Which of the nine adds ranked under both readings actually move life drained and kill-by-turn-8 on this list under Forge against standard-v3, with the paired cuts applied — and does cutting Conqueror (reading B) cost a measurable share of the 0.413 win rate (ci95 [0.283, 0.557], n=60) it was measured with?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A branch with `--objective` is the falsifiable form of this prescription; the objective should be an OUTPUT (damage or kill-by-turn), never an engine-membership axis, per the 2026-08-28 rule.
